When these logos first appeared.Twinings lion logo: Twinings has used the same lion-based logo since 1787, and the company says it is the oldest in continuous use.
When these logos first appeared.Bass red triangle: Bass's red triangle became the first trademark registered in the UK, on the first day the law allowed it.
When these logos first appeared.Shell scallop shell: The scallop shell refers to the pilgrim shells linked to the founder's family business, which began with trading seashells.
When these logos first appeared.Mercedes three-pointed star: The three points of the star stand for the company's aim to power transport on land, sea and air.
When these logos first appeared.Playboy bunny: The famous bunny in a bow tie was drawn by art director Art Paul and first appeared in 1953.
When these logos first appeared.Nike Swoosh: Designer Carolyn Davidson was a student when she created the Swoosh for just 35 dollars, and it now represents a vast company.
When these logos first appeared.Apple's bitten apple: The bite out of the apple helped distinguish it from a cherry, and the original rainbow stripes were removed years later.
When these logos first appeared.FedEx hidden arrow: Between the E and x of the FedEx name is a white arrow, which has won many design awards.
When these logos first appeared.Amazon smile arrow: The curved arrow underneath the name points from A to Z, suggesting that the company sells everything, and also looks like a smile.
When these logos first appeared.Twitter's current bird: The logo of the social media firm, called Larry the Bird, was later replaced by an X after a rebrand in 2023.

The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Red-billed hornbill: Zazu's species uses its big beak like tongs to pick insects and fruit, and nests in tree holes sealed shut with mud by the female.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Meerkat: Timon's kind take turns as sentries, standing on hind legs to watch for hawks, and live in groups called mobs.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Flamingo: Flamingos get their pink from carotenoid pigments in algae and shrimp, and they feed with their heads upside down.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Mandrill: Rafiki is a mandrill, the largest monkey in the world, and the male's blue and red face is brightest in dominant individuals.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Warthog: Pumbaa's species often kneels on its front knees to graze, and shelters in abandoned aardvark burrows, entering backwards.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Lion: Lions are the only truly social big cats, living in prides, and a male's mane darkens with age and with hormones.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Blue wildebeest: The stampede echoes the real Serengeti migration, where well over a million wildebeest follow the rains each year.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Plains zebra: No two zebras share the same stripe pattern, and the stripes may help discourage biting flies.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.Giraffe: A giraffe's neck has the same seven vertebrae as yours, each just far longer, and its heart weighs around 11 kg.
The Lion King cast, by real-life weight.African elephant: The heaviest land animal can eat around 150 kg of plants a day, and its trunk has tens of thousands of muscle units.

Countries of Oceania by area.Nauru: Third-smallest country on Earth after the Vatican and Monaco; its fortune came from phosphate mined from ancient seabird droppings.
Countries of Oceania by area.Palau: Its Jellyfish Lake is full of golden jellyfish that evolved to lose most of their sting, and in 2009 Palau created the first shark sanctuary.
Countries of Oceania by area.Kiribati: Its islands straddle both the equator and the 180th meridian, so in 1995 it bent the date line to keep the whole country on one day.
Countries of Oceania by area.Samoa: In 2011 Samoa jumped across the date line and skipped December 30 entirely, to line its calendar up with Australia and New Zealand.
Countries of Oceania by area.Vanuatu: Mount Yasur on Tanna island has erupted almost continuously for centuries, and Vanuatu's land divers inspired modern bungee jumping.
Countries of Oceania by area.Fiji: Its more than 300 islands include only about a third that are inhabited, and its Great Sea Reef is among the world's longest barrier reefs.
Countries of Oceania by area.Solomon Islands: Guadalcanal here saw a brutal 1942-43 World War II campaign, and the islands have around 70 languages.
Countries of Oceania by area.New Zealand: Its Māori name is Aotearoa, and before humans arrived the only native land mammals were bats.
Countries of Oceania by area.Papua New Guinea: With over 800 languages, it is the most linguistically diverse country on Earth, and it shares its main island with Indonesia.
Countries of Oceania by area.Australia: It is the only country that fills a whole continent, and kangaroos here are thought to outnumber people.

Famously brief: how long did it last?.Wright brothers' first flight: Orville Wright's flight covered about 37 meters, and later that day the longest of four flights lasted 59 seconds.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Hindenburg burning up: The airship burned in barely a minute at Lakehurst in 1937, killing 36 of the 97 on board.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Alan Shepard's spaceflight: Freedom 7 made him the first American in space, though only suborbital and weeks after Gagarin.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Anglo-Zanzibar War: Britain shelled the Sultan's palace, and the 1896 war is the shortest on record.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Gagarin's orbit: Vostok 1 circled the Earth once on April 12, 1961, and he reportedly said Poyekhali, let's go.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Titanic sinking: It sank about two hours and forty minutes after hitting the iceberg, with over 1,500 lives lost.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Britney Spears' first marriage: The pop star married a childhood friend in Las Vegas in 2004, and it was annulled.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Apollo 11 mission: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent about 21 hours on the Moon of this roughly week-long trip.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Mayflower crossing: The Mayflower sailed from England with 102 passengers in 1620 and made it to Cape Cod.
Famously brief: how long did it last?.Kardashian-Humphries marriage: The lavish 2011 televised wedding ended after only 72 days.

Milestones in the history of psychology.Wundt opens first psych lab: Wilhelm Wundt's 1879 lab in Leipzig is considered the birth of experimental psychology, and he trained many of its early leaders.
Milestones in the history of psychology.William James's Principles: His two-volume 1890 textbook gave psychology the phrase stream of consciousness and shaped the field for decades.
Milestones in the history of psychology.The Interpretation of Dreams: Freud's book was released in November 1899, though the publisher dated it 1900; it sold only a few hundred copies in its first years.
Milestones in the history of psychology.Binet-Simon intelligence test: Alfred Binet designed it to identify French schoolchildren who needed extra help, not to rank everyone by innate intelligence.
Milestones in the history of psychology.Rorschach inkblot test: Hermann Rorschach, a Swiss psychiatrist, published his ten inkblots in 1921 and died the next year, long before the test became famous.
Milestones in the history of psychology.Maslow's hierarchy of needs: Maslow never drew the pyramid himself; the triangle shape was added by later authors to illustrate his ideas.
Milestones in the history of psychology.First DSM published: The American Psychiatric Association's first manual listed about 100 disorders; modern editions list hundreds.
Milestones in the history of psychology.Kübler-Ross's five stages: Her five stages came from work with dying patients, not from people who were grieving, and she later said they are not a fixed sequence.
Milestones in the history of psychology.Prospect theory: Kahneman and Tversky showed losses sting about twice as much as equal gains please; Kahneman won the Nobel Prize in 2002.
Milestones in the history of psychology.Positive psychology launched: Martin Seligman made it his theme as president of the American Psychological Association in 1998, shifting focus from disorders to strengths.

Famous experiments, by when they happene.Eratosthenes measures Earth: He compared shadows in Syene and Alexandria to calculate Earth's circumference, coming within a modest margin of the real value.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Torricelli's barometer: His mercury tube created a vacuum and was the basis of the barometer; the pressure unit torr is named for him.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Franklin's kite: Whether he flew it is debated, but later copycat attempts killed Georg Richmann in 1753.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Cavendish weighs the Earth: Henry Cavendish used a torsion balance to find Earth's density, about 5.4 times that of water.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Foucault's pendulum: Hung in the Pantheon in Paris, the pendulum's swinging path shows the Earth rotates.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Michelson-Morley: They failed to find the luminiferous ether, which later helped Einstein's relativity.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Millikan's oil drop: He found the electron's charge by suspending oil droplets, and won the Nobel Prize in 1923.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Eddington's eclipse: Observing the 1919 solar eclipse, he found starlight bent by gravity as Einstein predicted, making Einstein world famous.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Miller-Urey experiment: Sparks through a flask mimicking early Earth created amino acids.
Famous experiments, by when they happene.Higgs boson found at CERN: Announced in July 2012 at CERN, 48 years after Peter Higgs predicted it; he shared the 2013 Nobel with Englert.

How tall these ancient structures stood.Stonehenge's tallest trilithon: Its biggest sarsen stones weigh about 25 tonnes each and were dragged roughly 25 km from the Marlborough Downs.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Statue of Zeus at Olympia: Phidias's seated statue of ivory and gold was among the Seven Wonders; it is said to have nearly touched the temple's roof.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Great Sphinx of Giza: Carved straight from limestone bedrock, it probably depicts pharaoh Khafre, and its missing nose was lost long ago.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Colossus of Rhodes: The bronze statue of the sun god Helios fell in an earthquake in 226 BC; the legend that it straddled the harbor is probably false.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Colosseum: It could seat about 50,000 spectators and had a retractable awning, hoisted by sailors, to shade the crowd.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Hagia Sophia (dome top): Built under Justinian in under six years, its enormous dome seems to float, thanks to a ring of windows at its base.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Pyramid of the Sun: Teotihuacan, in Mexico, is home to this giant; the name is Aztec, given centuries after the city was abandoned, and means birthplace of the gods.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Lighthouse of Alexandria: The Pharos stood on an island and became so famous that the word for lighthouse in several languages, such as French phare, comes from it.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Great Pyramid (original): The tallest human-made structure for roughly 3,800 years, it stayed on top until a medieval spire finally beat it.
How tall these ancient structures stood.Lincoln Cathedral, with spire: Its central spire, which collapsed in 1548, probably made it the world's tallest building around 1300, overtaking the Great Pyramid.

Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Absolute zero in °C: Nothing can be colder, since atoms nearly stop moving here; labs have cooled matter to within billionths of a degree of it.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.The golden ratio: Often said to hide in art and nature, its beauty is largely myth, but it truly emerges from ratios in the Fibonacci sequence.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Pi: Pi is irrational so its digits never repeat, and Pi Day on March 14 is also Albert Einstein's birthday.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.James Bond's 00 number: In Fleming's novels the double-0 prefix marks agents licensed to kill, and 007 is the most famous of that elite few.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Harry's King's Cross platform: Harry reaches the Hogwarts Express by running at a barrier in King's Cross, where fans can now pose with a luggage trolley half in the wall.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Hitchhiker's Guide answer: Douglas Adams said it was just a joke number, and the supercomputer Deep Thought took 7.5 million years to produce it.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Water's boiling point in °F: Water only boils at 212 degrees at sea level; higher up, thinner air lets it boil cooler, which changes cooking times.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Room in The Shining (film): In Kubrick's film this hotel room is the haunted one, but in Stephen King's book it was room 217, changed at a real hotel's request.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Web error 'Not Found': This code means the server was reached but the page is missing; the legend of a room at CERN behind its name is a myth.
Famous numbers, smallest to largest.Number of the Beast: Revelation names it the number of the beast, though some early manuscripts give 616 instead.

Primates on the scale.Gray mouse lemur: Small enough to sit in a human palm, this Madagascan primate enters torpor in the cool dry season, living off fat stored in its body.
Primates on the scale.Pygmy marmoset: The world's smallest monkey lives in Amazon treetops and gouges holes in bark with its teeth to feed on the sap and gum that leaks out.
Primates on the scale.Squirrel monkey: Squirrel monkeys have the largest brain relative to body size among primates, and they live in groups of dozens in tropical forests.
Primates on the scale.Ring-tailed lemur: The ring-tailed lemur's striped tail is used in 'stink fights', where males rub scent on it and then wave it at rivals.
Primates on the scale.Lar gibbon: Gibbons swing through trees using their long arms, and they sing duets between mates, and they are classed as lesser apes with no tail.
Primates on the scale.Japanese macaque: These monkeys of Japan soak in hot springs in winter, and they live further north than any other non-human primate.
Primates on the scale.Olive baboon (male): Male olive baboons have large canines and live in troops of up to 100 or more, and they are found across Africa.
Primates on the scale.Chimpanzee: Our closest living relative shares about 98 percent of our DNA, and it uses tools like twigs to fish for termites.
Primates on the scale.Orangutan (male): The name means 'person of the forest' in Malay, and adult males develop wide cheek pads called flanges, and they are the largest tree-living animals.
Primates on the scale.Gorilla (male): Males can weigh up to 200 kg, and they beat their chests, and they are mostly vegetarian, eating leaves, shoots and fruit.

Lakes by surface area.Loch Ness: Loch Ness is small by area but holds more water than all the lakes of England and Wales, since it is 230 m deep.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Geneva: Its crescent shape on the Swiss-French border makes it the largest lake in Western Europe, and Montreux's jazz festival is on its shore.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Titicaca: The highest navigable lake in the world, at about 3,800 m, straddles Peru and Bolivia, and its reed islands are home to the Uros people.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Ontario: The smallest of the Great Lakes by area receives Niagara Falls' water from Lake Erie, and it empties through the Saint Lawrence toward the Atlantic.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Erie: The shallowest and warmest of the Great Lakes, it freezes over more often than the others, and sometimes does so almost completely.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Tanganyika: This African Great Lake is the longest freshwater lake on Earth, at about 670 km, and the second deepest.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Huron: Guinness recognized her as the most married woman, with 23 marriages, and her last husband, Glynn Wolfe, was the record-holding most-married man.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Victoria: Africa's biggest lake, and the main source of the White Nile, it is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania.
Lakes by surface area.Lake Superior: The world's largest freshwater lake by surface area, it holds about 10 percent of the planet's surface fresh water.
Lakes by surface area.Caspian Sea: The largest inland body of water, it is called a sea because of its size and saltiness, and it is home to most of the world's caviar-producing sturgeon.

One lap of these tracks.Short track skating oval: Short track skating ovals are tiny, and sharp corners are where much of the sport's action, and falls, happen.
One lap of these tracks.Olympic velodrome: Velodromes are banked at up to about 42 degrees, which is why cyclists can lean in and ride in the steep turns.
One lap of these tracks.Athletics track: A standard track is 400 meters, so a 'quarter mile' race is only a bit longer than a lap, which is why it was once called a lap of a quarter mile.
One lap of these tracks.Bristol Motor Speedway: Bristol, nicknamed 'the Last Great Colosseum', is a short concrete-banked oval in Tennessee famed for close, bumping races.
One lap of these tracks.Monaco GP circuit: Monaco is slow and narrow, yet it hosts a grand prix where qualifying position matters more than at almost any other track.
One lap of these tracks.Indianapolis oval: The Indianapolis oval is nicknamed 'the Brickyard' because it was once paved with 3.2 million bricks, and a yard of them is kept as a finish line.
One lap of these tracks.Spa-Francorchamps: Spa-Francorchamps in Belgium is famous for the Eau Rouge corner, and for weather that can be rainy on one part of the track and dry on another.
One lap of these tracks.Le Mans circuit: Le Mans is a lap made up of closed public roads and a permanent circuit, and the full lap includes the long Mulsanne Straight.
One lap of these tracks.Nurburgring Nordschleife: The Nordschleife, nicknamed 'the Green Hell' by Jackie Stewart, has about 150 corners and is used by manufacturers to test cars.
One lap of these tracks.Isle of Man TT course: The Isle of Man TT is run on ordinary public roads with stone walls and houses close by, making it among the most dangerous races in the world.

Olympic medal debut of these sports.Basketball: James Naismith invented it in 1891 with a soccer ball and peach baskets, and at the 1936 Games it was played outdoors on tennis courts.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Volleyball: William Morgan invented the game in 1895 as a gentler indoor sport for older businessmen, and he first called it Mintonette.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Indoor handball: An outdoor 11-a-side version appeared in 1936 before the indoor seven-player game took over, after which the older one faded away.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Table tennis: It began as a Victorian parlor game called ping-pong, and the sport's fastest players can hit the ball at over 100 km/h.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Badminton: It is named after Badminton House in Gloucestershire, and smashes with the shuttlecock exceed 500 km/h, making it the fastest racket sport.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Beach volleyball: The game began on California beaches in the 1920s, and a two-person format is played on sand about 8 m by 16 m.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Triathlon: The sport was invented in 1970s San Diego, and Sydney 2000 was its Olympic debut, with swimming, cycling and running done back to back.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.BMX racing: It began in 1970s California, when children raced motocross-style on dirt tracks, inspired by the movie On Any Sunday.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Rugby sevens: Ned Haig invented it in Melrose, Scotland, in 1883 as a quick fundraising version of rugby, with seven players and short halves.
Olympic medal debut of these sports.Breaking: Born in the Bronx in the 1970s as part of hip-hop culture, it made its Olympic debut at the 2024 Paris Games.

Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Vaseline: Robert Chesebrough discovered it after seeing oil rig workers use rod wax to heal cuts.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Listerine: It was named after Joseph Lister, the pioneer of antiseptic surgery.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Bayer Aspirin: Felix Hoffmann at Bayer made it, based on chemicals from willow bark that had been used for pain for centuries.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Band-Aid: Earle Dickson, a Johnson and Johnson employee, invented it for his wife, who often cut her fingers.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Q-tips: Leo Gerstenzang got the idea from watching his wife wrap cotton around toothpicks.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Alka-Seltzer: Its fizzing tablets contain aspirin, and the Plop plop fizz fizz ad is famous.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Benadryl: It was the first antihistamine of its kind approved in the US.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Tylenol: Poisoned bottles in 1982 led to the tamper-proof packaging used on medicines today.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Advil: It was developed by Boots in the UK, where the ibuprofen was first developed in the 1960s.
Medicine cabinet staples, by debut.Claritin: It is a non-drowsy antihistamine, and its generic name is loratadine.

When these epidemics broke out.Great Plague of London: Samuel Pepys wrote about it in his diary; it killed perhaps a fifth of London's people and faded before the Great Fire of 1666.
When these epidemics broke out.Great Plague of Marseille: It began when the ship Grand-Saint-Antoine docked from the Levant, and it was the last major plague outbreak in western Europe.
When these epidemics broke out.First cholera pandemic: It began in Bengal and spread across Asia; decades later John Snow's work on a London pump showed that cholera spreads through water.
When these epidemics broke out.Third plague pandemic: It began in China's Yunnan, reached Hong Kong in 1894, where Alexandre Yersin identified the plague bacterium, and killed over 12 million.
When these epidemics broke out.Spanish flu: It was called Spanish only because neutral Spain reported on it freely under wartime censorship; it infected about a third of the world.
When these epidemics broke out.Asian flu: An H2N2 virus from China, it prompted a vaccine within months and then vanished from circulation once H3N2 took over in 1968.
When these epidemics broke out.Hong Kong flu: Caused by H3N2, it killed around a million people worldwide, and its descendants still circulate as seasonal flu today.
When these epidemics broke out.AIDS first identified: A 1981 report of unusual pneumonia in young men in Los Angeles signalled it; HIV was identified as the cause by 1983.
When these epidemics broke out.SARS: It emerged in southern China in late 2002, then spread to dozens of countries and caused about 8,000 cases before isolation measures contained it.
When these epidemics broke out.Swine flu: Declared a pandemic by the WHO, this H1N1 strain combined genes from swine, bird and human flu, and was the first flu pandemic in over 40 years.

The life of Moses, in story order.Set adrift in a basket: In Exodus the basket was sealed with tar and pitch and hidden in the reeds of the Nile.
The life of Moses, in story order.Adopted by Pharaoh's daughter: The story explains his name as 'drawn out' of the water, though an Egyptian word 'mose' means 'born of'.
The life of Moses, in story order.Kills an Egyptian: He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew slave, killed him and hid the body in the sand.
The life of Moses, in story order.Flees to Midian: There he married Zipporah, daughter of the priest Jethro, and tradition says he worked as a shepherd for 40 years.
The life of Moses, in story order.The burning bush: At Mount Horeb a bush burned without being consumed, and a voice told Moses to return to Egypt.
The life of Moses, in story order.Ten plagues: They include the Nile turned to blood, frogs, locusts and the death of the firstborn, which Passover recalls.
The life of Moses, in story order.Crossing the Red Sea: The Hebrew name Yam Suf literally means 'Sea of Reeds', and scholars still debate where it was.
The life of Moses, in story order.Receives the Ten Commandments: Received at Mount Sinai on two stone tablets, the event is celebrated in Judaism on Shavuot.
The life of Moses, in story order.The golden calf: While Moses was on the mountain, Aaron made the idol, and Moses smashed the tablets in anger.
The life of Moses, in story order.Dies on Mount Nebo: Moses saw the Promised Land from this mountain, which stands in modern Jordan, but wasn't allowed to enter.

How many Oscars did each film win?.Spotlight: It tells of the Boston Globe's investigation into abuse in the Catholic Church, and won Best Picture and Best Original Screenplay.
How many Oscars did each film win?.Rocky: Stallone reportedly wrote the script in just a few days, and insisted on starring in it rather than selling it to a star.
How many Oscars did each film win?.Parasite: It was the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture, and Bong Joon-ho thanked his director idol Scorsese in his speech.
How many Oscars did each film win?.The Silence of the Lambs: Hannibal Lecter appears for only around 16 minutes, yet it swept all five top categories, a feat achieved by only three films.
How many Oscars did each film win?.Mad Max: Fury Road: All six of its wins were in technical categories, including film editing, costume design and production design.
How many Oscars did each film win?.Schindler's List: Spielberg won his first Best Director for it, and he shot it in black and white, with little use of a score.
How many Oscars did each film win?.Gandhi: Costume designer Bhanu Athaiya became India's first Oscar winner for it, sharing the award with John Mollo.
How many Oscars did each film win?.The Last Emperor: It won every one of its nine nominations, and was the first Western film permitted to shoot inside the Forbidden City.
How many Oscars did each film win?.West Side Story (1961): Rita Moreno became the first Latina to win an acting Oscar, for playing Anita, and she later became an EGOT winner.
How many Oscars did each film win?.Ben-Hur: Its record of 11 Oscars is shared with Titanic and The Return of the King, and its chariot race cost a fortune to film.

Antarctic animals by weight.Antarctic midge: This tiny wingless fly is the largest purely land animal in Antarctica, and it lives nowhere else.
Antarctic animals by weight.Antarctic krill: Swarms of this shrimp-like creature are so enormous that their total mass is among the greatest of any animal species.
Antarctic animals by weight.Snow petrel: Pure white, it breeds farther south than any other bird, nesting on bare mountains far from the coast.
Antarctic animals by weight.Adélie penguin: Named by Dumont d'Urville for his wife Adèle, these penguins nest in huge colonies on rocky shores.
Antarctic animals by weight.Wandering albatross: Its wingspan is the longest of any living bird, reaching about 3.5 meters.
Antarctic animals by weight.Emperor penguin: Males balance the single egg on their feet for about two months through the Antarctic winter.
Antarctic animals by weight.Leopard seal: A top predator with a snake-like head, it hunts penguins and seals and is the penguin's greatest threat.
Antarctic animals by weight.Southern elephant seal (male): Males are named for their inflatable nose, which they use to produce roars during fights.
Antarctic animals by weight.Humpback whale: Males sing long songs, and each year the whales migrate from polar feeding waters to warm breeding grounds.
Antarctic animals by weight.Blue whale: The largest animal ever known, its calls reach around 180 decibels, among the loudest sounds any animal makes.

Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-97: This is one of the shortest Interstates, a short spur in Maryland that runs between Baltimore and Annapolis.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-5: The longest north-south highway on the West Coast runs from Mexico to Canada through California, Oregon and Washington.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-35: This highway links Laredo, Texas, to Duluth, Minnesota, and it splits into two near Dallas and Minneapolis.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-75: I-75 runs from the Canadian border in Michigan to Miami, and it crosses the Everglades on a stretch nicknamed Alligator Alley.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-95: The main East Coast highway, running from Maine to Miami, passes through Boston, New York and Washington.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-70: I-70 runs from Utah to Maryland, and the stretch through Colorado's Glenwood Canyon is considered an engineering marvel.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-10: I-10 runs from California to Florida, and it is the southernmost cross-country Interstate.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-40: I-40 runs from California to North Carolina and replaces much of the old Route 66 in places.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-80: I-80 runs from the San Francisco Bay Area to New Jersey, and it crosses the Sierra Nevada via Donner Pass.
Lengths of US Interstate highways.I-90: The longest Interstate in the US runs from Seattle to Boston, and it includes the Massachusetts Turnpike.

Playwrights, by birth year.Sophocles: Of roughly 120 plays, only seven survive complete, including Oedipus Rex.
Playwrights, by birth year.William Shakespeare: About half of his plays first appeared in print in the First Folio of 1623, seven years after he died.
Playwrights, by birth year.Molière: Born Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, he collapsed during a performance of The Imaginary Invalid and died hours later.
Playwrights, by birth year.Henrik Ibsen: A Doll's House ended with Nora walking out the door, a shock to 1879 audiences.
Playwrights, by birth year.Oscar Wilde: The Importance of Being Earnest came out in 1895; Wilde was an Irishman who also wrote fairy tales.
Playwrights, by birth year.Anton Chekhov: He was also a physician, and said medicine was his wife and literature his mistress.
Playwrights, by birth year.Eugene O'Neill: The only American playwright to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1936), and he won four Pulitzers.
Playwrights, by birth year.Samuel Beckett: Waiting for Godot made the Irishman famous; he won the Nobel Prize in 1969.
Playwrights, by birth year.Tennessee Williams: Born Thomas Lanier Williams, he wrote A Streetcar Named Desire and The Glass Menagerie.
Playwrights, by birth year.Arthur Miller: The Crucible used the Salem witch trials to criticise McCarthyism; he was also once married to Marilyn Monroe.

Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Thales of Miletus: Often called the first philosopher, he sought natural rather than divine explanations, and is said to have predicted an eclipse.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Pythagoras: His followers lived like a secret brotherhood with odd rules; the theorem named for him was already known in Babylon.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Democritus: He proposed that everything is made of indivisible 'atomos' moving in empty space, an idea revived two millennia later.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Archimedes: He worked out buoyancy and the lever, and was killed when Romans captured his home city of Syracuse.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Ptolemy: His Almagest laid out an Earth-centered cosmos that dominated astronomy for about 1,400 years.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Brahmagupta: This Indian mathematician gave the first clear rules for arithmetic with zero and negative numbers.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Al-Khwarizmi: His name gave us 'algorithm', and the title of his book al-jabr gave us 'algebra'.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen): His Book of Optics showed that we see by light entering the eye, and he is credited as an early champion of experiment.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Fibonacci: He brought Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe in Liber Abaci, and a rabbit-breeding puzzle there gave us the Fibonacci sequence.
Ancient and medieval scholars, by birth.Roger Bacon: A Franciscan friar who championed experiment and observation, he wrote about lenses, spectacles and gunpowder.

First close-up visits to small worlds.Halley's Comet: The European probe passed within about 600 km of the nucleus, which turned out to be as dark as coal.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Gaspra: The first asteroid ever photographed up close, it was seen by a Jupiter-bound probe on its way.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Ida: The same probe discovered that this asteroid has its own tiny moon, named Dactyl.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Mathilde: The probe found it to be coal-black and covered with huge craters, with a surprisingly low density.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Comet Borrelly: The first spacecraft powered by ion engines to visit a comet, it found a roughly peanut-shaped nucleus.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Comet Wild 2: The probe gathered dust from the comet's coma and returned it to Earth in 2006, a first for a comet.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Comet Tempel 1: A probe slammed a copper impactor into it on July 4, creating a dust cloud to peek inside.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Lutetia: A European probe passed this big asteroid, about 100 km across, on its way to a comet.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Toutatis: China's lunar orbiter, on an extended mission, flew by this potato-shaped near-Earth asteroid.
First close-up visits to small worlds.Dinkinesh: The NASA probe found it was a tiny binary pair, and its name means "you are marvelous" in Amharic.

Named after people: when they hit histor.Silhouette: Étienne de Silhouette was France's finance minister, and his austerity measures made cheap black paper profiles mock-able as 'à la Silhouette'.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Sandwich: John Montagu, Earl of Sandwich, is said to have asked for meat between bread so he could keep playing cards without leaving the table.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Guillotine: Doctor Joseph-Ignace Guillotin did not invent the device; he proposed it as a more humane way of executing people.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Saxophone: Adolphe Sax, a Belgian instrument maker, invented the saxophone, and he survived several accidents, including poisoning.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Boycott: Captain Charles Boycott was an estate manager in Ireland whose tenants shunned him in a land dispute, creating the word.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Ferris wheel: George Washington Gale Ferris Jr. built the first one for the Chicago World's Fair, to rival the Eiffel Tower.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Zeppelin: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin built rigid airships in Germany, and his name became synonymous with airships, and a rock band.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Biro: László Bíró, a Hungarian journalist, invented the ballpoint pen after noticing that newspaper ink dried quickly.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Tupperware: The brand is named after the Earl Tupper, who made plastic containers with an airtight seal, and sold via home parties.
Named after people: when they hit histor.Jacuzzi: Roy Jacuzzi invented the whirlpool bath for his son who had arthritis, and the family's company began with farm pumps.

Firsts in the history of surgery.Amyand's appendectomy: Claudius Amyand removed an appendix from a boy in London, and he found it inside a hernia, the first known successful appendectomy.
Firsts in the history of surgery.McDowell ovarian tumor surgery: Ephraim McDowell in Kentucky removed a huge ovarian tumor without anesthesia or antiseptics, and the patient lived 30 more years.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Lister's carbolic acid: Joseph Lister's carbolic acid spray dramatically cut deaths after operations, and led to modern sterile surgery.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Rubber surgical gloves: William Halsted had them made by Goodyear for his nurse's sensitive skin, and she later became his wife.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Rehn sutures a stabbed heart: Ludwig Rehn successfully sewed up a stab wound in a beating heart, which was previously thought to be impossible.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Carrel's blood vessel stitch: Alexis Carrel's method of joining blood vessels won him a Nobel Prize and made organ transplants possible.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Heart-lung machine surgery: John Gibbon's device took over the work of the heart and lungs, letting surgeons operate on a still, empty heart.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Charnley's hip replacement: John Charnley's design used a metal ball and plastic socket held in place with bone cement, and it is the basis of modern hip replacements.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Keyhole gallbladder surgery: The first laparoscopic cholecystectomy, by Erich Mühe in Germany, started a revolution in surgery with small cuts.
Firsts in the history of surgery.Transatlantic remote surgery: In the Lindbergh Operation, surgeons in New York removed a gallbladder from a patient in Strasbourg, France, using robotic arms.

Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Smallpox vaccine (Jenner): Edward Jenner tested cowpox on a boy, James Phipps. Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Ether anesthesia demo: William Morton's demonstration at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston showed painless surgery was possible.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Antiseptic surgery (Lister): Joseph Lister sprayed carbolic acid on wounds and instruments, cutting deadly infections.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.X-rays discovered: Wilhelm Röntgen's discovery was used within months to find bullets inside wounded soldiers.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Insulin isolated: Banting and Best in Toronto sold the patent for just one dollar each so it would stay affordable.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Penicillin discovered: Fleming spotted it in 1928, but Florey and Chain turned it into a mass-produced drug in World War II.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Salk polio vaccine: The field trial for Jonas Salk's vaccine involved about 1.8 million American children.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.First heart transplant: Surgeon Christiaan Barnard did it in Cape Town. His patient, Louis Washkansky, lived 18 days.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.First IVF baby: Louise Brown was born in England in 1978. Robert Edwards won a Nobel Prize for IVF in 2010.
Big medical breakthroughs, in order.Dolly the sheep cloned: Cloned from a mammary-gland cell and named after Dolly Parton, she lived to age six.

Number systems, by their base.Binary: Base 2 uses only 0 and 1, which map to a switch being off or on. Leibniz described it in the 1600s, long before computers.
Number systems, by their base.Ternary: The Soviet Setun computer of 1958 was built around base three. Ternary logic is rare in computing today.
Number systems, by their base.Quaternary: Four digits suit the four letters of DNA's genetic code. Biologists often think of DNA as a quaternary system.
Number systems, by their base.Quinary: Base five arose from counting on one hand. The Roman numeral V is said to resemble a hand with the thumb spread.
Number systems, by their base.Octal: Octal is used in Unix file permissions, like chmod 755. Each digit packs three binary bits neatly.
Number systems, by their base.Decimal: Humans likely adopted base ten because we have ten fingers. Nearly all modern cultures use it for everyday counting.
Number systems, by their base.Duodecimal: Twelve divides by 2, 3, 4 and 6, which explains a dozen eggs and 12 inches in a foot. Some mathematicians prefer it to base ten.
Number systems, by their base.Hexadecimal: Programmers use hex because one digit is exactly four bits. Web colours like #FF0000 are written in it.
Number systems, by their base.Vigesimal: The Maya used base 20, and the French say "quatre-vingts" (four twenties) for 80. Counting fingers and toes may explain it.
Number systems, by their base.Sexagesimal: The Babylonians used base 60, and we still do for 60 minutes in an hour and 360 degrees in a circle.

When these great libraries were founded.Library of Ashurbanipal: Nineveh's king gathered tablets, including the Epic of Gilgamesh.
When these great libraries were founded.Plato's Academy: The name was later reused for the word 'academy', and Aristotle studied here.
When these great libraries were founded.Aristotle's Lyceum: Aristotle taught while walking around, so his followers were called 'peripatetic'.
When these great libraries were founded.Library of Alexandria: Ptolemy's goal was to collect every scroll, and ships were searched for books to copy.
When these great libraries were founded.Library of Pergamum: A rival to Alexandria, and parchment is named after the city.
When these great libraries were founded.Library of Celsus, Ephesus: Built as a tomb for Celsus, its facade was reconstructed after earthquakes.
When these great libraries were founded.Nalanda: This ancient Buddhist university in India drew students like the Chinese monk Xuanzang.
When these great libraries were founded.House of Wisdom, Baghdad: Under Abbasid caliphs, scholars translated Greek works into Arabic here.
When these great libraries were founded.Library of Córdoba: Reportedly held hundreds of thousands of volumes under caliph al-Hakam II.
When these great libraries were founded.Vatican Library: Pope Sixtus IV formally founded it, and it is among the oldest libraries in Europe.

Launch prices of Apple gear.AirPods: Its 2016 launch came with a wireless design, and its tiny design kept growing, with sales soon in the tens of millions.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Apple Watch Sport: The gold Edition model cost up to $17,000, much more than this basic sport version.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Original iPod: Apple promised 'a thousand songs in your pocket' in 2001, with a 5 GB drive.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Original iPad: Steve Jobs unveiled it in 2010 as something between a phone and a laptop.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Original iPhone (8 GB): Two months after launch, Apple cut its price by $200, angering early buyers, and then gave them $100 credit.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Apple I: Steve Wozniak liked repeating digits, and the hand-built board has about 200 units made.
Launch prices of Apple gear.IBM PC (rival): Apple welcomed IBM into the personal computer market with a full-page newspaper ad reading 'Welcome, IBM. Seriously.'
Launch prices of Apple gear.Macintosh 128K: Apple introduced it with a famous Ridley Scott-directed ad in the 1984 Super Bowl.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Vision Pro: Apple's headset launched in early 2024, a giant leap for a company that had lost sleep about weight and cost.
Launch prices of Apple gear.Apple Lisa: The first commercial computer with a mouse and graphical interface was a flop, and unsold units were reportedly buried in a Utah landfill.

How long these light sources last.Burning match: Safety matches ignite only on the box, since the red phosphorus sits on the striker strip.
How long these light sources last.Sparkler: Sparklers burn above 1,000 degrees Celsius, which is why they cause many children's firework burns.
How long these light sources last.Birthday candle: The tradition of birthday candles is often traced back to German children's celebrations.
How long these light sources last.Tealight: It gets its name from the tea warmers it once heated, and its metal cup lets wax pool.
How long these light sources last.Glow stick: It makes light through a chemical reaction without heat, and glows brighter when warm and dimmer when cold.
How long these light sources last.Pillar candle: Trimming the wick to about a quarter inch keeps it from smoking and helps it last.
How long these light sources last.Incandescent bulb: A bulb in Livermore, California, has been burning almost without interruption since 1901.
How long these light sources last.Halogen bulb: Touching it with bare fingers can leave oil that makes hot spots and breaks the bulb.
How long these light sources last.CFL bulb: It contains a small amount of mercury, so needs careful disposal.
How long these light sources last.LED bulb: At three hours a day, 25,000 hours is about 23 years, and the blue LED earned a 2014 Nobel Prize.

England's royal houses: when each took o.Normans: William's conquest was followed by the Domesday Book in 1086, a survey of England's land.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Plantagenets: Their name probably comes from the sprig of broom, planta genista, Geoffrey of Anjou wore.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Lancaster: Henry IV seized the throne from Richard II, with a red rose as the family badge.
England's royal houses: when each took o.York: Edward IV took the throne in the Wars of the Roses, with a white rose as the family badge.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Tudors: Henry VII won at Bosworth Field, and the dynasty ended with Elizabeth I in 1603.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Stuarts: James VI of Scotland became James I of England, uniting the crowns.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Commonwealth (no monarch): After Charles I was executed, Oliver Cromwell ruled as Lord Protector until the monarchy returned in 1660.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Hanover: George I, who barely spoke English, came from Germany because Queen Anne left no surviving heir.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Saxe-Coburg and Gotha: Named for Prince Albert's family, only one monarch, Edward VII, reigned under it.
England's royal houses: when each took o.Windsor: George V changed the family name in World War I to drop the German-sounding Saxe-Coburg.

Famous written works, by when they were.Code of Hammurabi: This Babylonian law code, carved on a black stone pillar, includes the famous eye-for-an-eye idea. It is one of the oldest long legal texts known.
Famous written works, by when they were.The Iliad: Attributed to Homer, it covers just a few weeks of the Trojan War, not the whole conflict. It was spread by memory and song before being written.
Famous written works, by when they were.Rosetta Stone: The same decree carved in three scripts let Jean-François Champollion crack Egyptian hieroglyphs in the 1820s. It is now in the British Museum.
Famous written works, by when they were.Book of Kells: An illuminated Gospel manuscript made by Celtic monks, packed with intricate swirls, animals and tiny details. It is kept at Trinity College Dublin.
Famous written works, by when they were.The Tale of Genji: Written by the court lady Murasaki Shikibu in Japan, it is often called the world's first novel. It follows the loves of a prince at the Heian court.
Famous written works, by when they were.Domesday Book: William the Conqueror ordered this great survey of England so he could tax it properly. The name suggests that, like Judgement Day, its verdicts could not be appealed.
Famous written works, by when they were.Magna Carta: King John sealed it at Runnymede under pressure from rebellious barons. It limited royal power and became a symbol of the rule of law.
Famous written works, by when they were.The Canterbury Tales: Chaucer left it unfinished, with 24 tales instead of the roughly 120 he planned. It is among the first major works written in English, not French or Latin.
Famous written works, by when they were.Gutenberg Bible: The first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type, and about 180 copies were made. Surviving copies now sell for millions.
Famous written works, by when they were.Don Quixote: Cervantes's tale of a knight who reads too many romances is often called the first modern novel. Its hero gave English the word quixotic.
